## Source: amazon-inspector (9300d6b1357396fa416b67a6b22b3d44108b517a6a3de83ea88788292bbcb2e9)
The published tarball of @adminide-stack/forms-core@5.1.9-alpha.3 ships a lib/index.js (the package main) whose top-level content diverges from the declared source and build. src/index.ts is a 10-line re-export module and rollup.config.mjs produces plain ES re-exports, but lib/index.js prepends a ~16 KB IIFE invoked as `})(global, require);` that stashes `require` and `module` onto `global` via property names reconstructed from a custom string-shuffle routine (`spin`/`splitLane`/`peel` driven by NX/SX constant arrays), deshuffles the string "constructor" to obtain `Function` from an object reference (`Forge = peel[ctor]`), and invokes `new Function` with a deshuffled ~15 KB code body: `Forge('z', peel("[...]"))(z);`. The construct runs at import/require time with full Node capabilities (require, fs, net) available via the stashed `require`. The gap between declared source plus build config and the shipped main, combined with hand-written string deobfuscation of control identifiers and an executable payload, is the fingerprint of a payload injected into the published artifact after or outside the declared build pipeline.

## Source: ghsa-malware (6b9e3f519363694211241ddf83d95c5f75a4f22ef9b5f60e2e962c01f97ddd25)
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.
